text: Continuous integration is a software development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each time new code is added, the system automatically runs a build to compile everything and checks for problems. Running tests is a crucial part of this process, as it helps developers catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. These steps are organized into CI pipelines, which are automated workflows that build, test, and validate code every time changes are made. This approach saves time and ensures that software remains stable and reliable throughout development.
